title: deputyOS network policy
description: Schema for /etc/deputyos/network-policy.json — the single source of truth for the device's network-egress posture. Read + mutated by `deputyctl network` and rendered into an nftables ruleset (/etc/nftables.conf) by the Ansible role. On an AIRGAP=1 build the airgap baseline drops a file with mode=airgap + set_at_build_time=true. Schema version 1; bump on breaking changes.

$schema.description: JSON Schema URL. Written so editors + future consumers can validate. The `deputyctl::network::Policy` struct defaults this when absent.

mode.description: Egress posture. `open` = unrestricted (the default for non-airgap builds). `whitelist` = allow only `allow_hosts`, enforced by an nftables output chain `policy drop` plus a resolved-IP allow rule per host (see the egress threat model for the DNS-only, not-SNI limitation). `airgap` = deny everything except RFC1918 + mDNS + the local DNS resolver.

allow_hosts.description: Hosts permitted in `whitelist` mode. Ignored in `open` (no restriction) and `airgap` (deny-by-default) modes. Entries are free-form hostnames or IPs the operator chose to allow.

set_at_build_time.description: True if the policy was written by the image bake (the airgap baseline). Flipped to false the first time the operator mutates it via `deputyctl network …`, so the dashboard can distinguish baked from hand-edited.

tier.description: Bake-time tier the policy was written for (e.g. lean, standard, rich). Informational; set by the airgap baseline.

hw.description: Bake-time hardware target (e.g. rpi4, qemu-aarch64). Informational; set by the airgap baseline.

profile.description: Active profile id the policy was written for (e.g. openclaw). Informational; set by the airgap baseline.
